followUpSession.role: Sub-agent of the T3 thread 'Audit Open PRs and Issues' (7f1c73c8-4f6e-4a8b-b5ff-8a57103912ce) that wrote 335c502 after Michael asked to route the workflows import through the product facade.

taskStatement:
![image.png](t3-context://v1/image/image_fd0a47cc-4bd9-4139-b4be-163b45289f9e) 
Add a workflows quick button under the home screen search box, and let's also brainstorm some suggestions here, which you could query for:
- Getting a list of existing workflows
- Maybe last email runs
- Creating new workflows
We give a new entry point for users and potentially increase growth and onboarding to our workflows product.
taskStatementNotes: Kept message 0 whole: it defines the feature (a Workflows quick button under the home search box, plus prompts the agent can answer: list workflows, recent email runs, create workflows). Dropped message 1 (1f2525e1, 'Cool, sounds good. Let's file the PR, but exclude the AI prompts that don't work right now. ...'). It approves a proposal the agent made after building the button: the in-app agent could not answer three of the four suggested prompts, so the agent offered a follow-up PR that teaches it to search and list workflows. That follow-up is #103523. The message's requirement, 'exclude the AI prompts that don't work right now', changed the prompts shipped in #103522. Both the approval and the requirement only make sense against the agent's proposal, which a replay does not see, so the message is not part of the statement. Dropped message 3 (77ded5fc, 'For the stacked second PR, let's disconnect it. ... we remove the question from the home menu ...'): it only makes #103522 and #103523 shippable independently, which does not apply to a single-diff replay. Dropped messages 2 (retry commit signing) and 4 (Slack bullet list): pure process. Caveat for scoring: message 0 asks for the home button and prompts; it does not ask to extend the in-app agent. That half of the historical work came from the agent's proposal and Michael's approval. The like-for-like Arm A reference for this statement is sessionAnswerDiff (both halves on one base); #103523's final diff is the agent half only, and it carries the facade signal.
whyChosen: Crosses a product boundary: the AI agent (ee/hogai) gains a workflows entity, and its first commit imported workflows models directly instead of going through products/workflows/backend/facade (fixed in 335c502).
notes: baseCommit 29bb275 is the merge-base with upstream master of the first pushed commit e39a5bc (2026-09-21 04:43Z). The T3 worktree started on the fork's master f637db9 (upstream 7b46385 plus one fork-only agent-config commit), and the agent branched feat/workflows-home-badge from the local upstream/master 29bb275 before its first commit; feat/agent-workflows-entity was stacked on it. That ref was last fetched on 2026-09-18, so the base is about 2.5 days older than upstream master was when the session started (cea129a, 2026-09-21 01:49Z). A second head, 75951bd ('fix(homepage): ask for draft workflows in the review prompt'), was pushed on top of e39a5bc at 05:32Z. The first commit's parent differs from baseCommit: when Michael asked to disconnect the stack (05:40Z), the agent rebuilt the branch as d8e4fa0 on upstream master cea129a and force-pushed it over 75951bd at 05:41Z, dropping the homepage change. GitHub's baseRefOid 8872766 is master at the last merge-from-master (2026-09-23), not the start point. firstPushHead e39a5bc sits on cffe971 (the original #103522 badge commit), so diffStat.firstPush covers both halves of the statement. d8e4fa0 imported products.workflows.backend.models.HogFlow into ee/hogai directly; the required Django CI failed, Michael asked to route the import through the product facade, and a Codex sub-agent did so in 335c502 (new facade functions, a facade testing helper and a tach.toml line). The final diff is merge-base(baseRefOid, finalHead)..finalHead, which equals the PR's GitHub diff.
